I think it appears to be disabled due to the lack of size uniformity. If we could get the font at the same size and only have initials capitalized, it should look smoother. If not, we can also go with a lighter gray.

Yes, @ShendMikullovci - I agree that the controls are inconsistent.

i've just been googling "toggle or switch" - and it appears a "Switch" control would be more suited to "Show archived lessons".  I _think_ we also need to make "Mark all as read" look more like a button.   I propose we give "Mark all as read" a border.  I also propose (as Shend said) we make the case consistent for both.

Let's remove the `Filter` control.  We really need per-column drop-down filters and `order` controls.  @lebaphi is going to experiment with this in the `Player log table` feature.

Could you produce an updated UI please @ShendMikullovci ?

Note: I know @ShendMikullovci is trying to reduce the visual clutter, but I'm pretty sure we can't use grey for these controls, since it's the standard way of indicating something is disabled:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/150954297-623ec968-0b61-4cb7-91f3-e06b4a7a23df.png)

I _guess_ another way of reducing the clutter would be to use smaller/simpler controls.  _Maybe_ we can come up with icons for "Show archived" and "Mark all as read" - with tooltips to give further explanation.

I'm very much pro turning these features into buttons. I had a go at it: 

![Inbox Icons](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/151068816-b4c7eb4c-b4f3-418b-a5d1-3fff8d69574f.png)

3 icons for all 3 features. The search "spyglass" icon is switched to a funnel icon since it more appropriately matches the term "filter". The archive button (middle) is the standard button for most messaging apps and is easily recognizable. Finally, the mark-read button we've used previously to maintain uniformity. 
In this screenshot, none of the features would be active.

In the screenshot below, all 3 features are active: 

![Inbox Icons 2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/151069326-225d5c28-7d7b-47b3-9dff-cfeb0efb51f7.png)

Here, the user has selected to mark all messages as read (sorry that I couldn't do it for a better illustration, bug), has selected to show archived (thus archive button is filled) and has clicked on the filter button to type what they're searching for. 
Personally, I'd consider using terms like "search" or "sort" for the latter feature.

issues.title: Font Size and Type Uniformity
issues.body:
Throughout many pages and windows of the game, the font size and type are somewhat inconsistent. It would be nice to have font uniformity through the different pages and windows.

Here's an example of different sizes of fonts in the same window:
![Different Size-Type Fonts](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/142914506-d9859c37-c791-430a-929f-650ca53aac4a.png)

comments.body: We have `Mark all as read` in 2 different font-sizes.  I don't really mind which size we use - but they should be the same size.  The left-hand window is probably "BLUE COA".

I agree. I suggest we use a slightly smaller font size than that of the "Mark all as read" on the right-hand side of the screenshot. Capitalization is great for visibility but with all the notifications and messages that will be filling up the screen, maybe it would be smoother to not have everything capitalized. 

Should I play around with some designs to see how it all looks?

@ShendMikullovci - could we go for a quick size decision, and defer the deeper analysis for the future please? I'll create a future [task](https://github.com/serge-web/serge/issues/1238) for you to investigate/consider use of fonts & font-case in Serge UI.   I'll label tasks like that as "UX - low priority", and you can work on them if/when there is nothing higher priority to do.
Great. I'll go through Serge screens and collect the different font sizes and see if I can come with a mean size.

I went through some of the pages of Serge. All of them have a variety of font types and sizes. 
Bold fonts should be used for titles and headers (also potentially important info in-screen, we'll see along the way).
The font I suggest we use is the following: 
![Font to Use](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/145615300-cfd36f53-489f-49a2-820e-eba63560d3a8.png)

I would also suggest that "Show archived" and both "Mark all read" buttons (one of them is Mark All As Read and the other is Mark All Read; I suggest both should be Mark All Read) be grey. They're not crucial to gameplay and don't need to take up attentional resources. We could use the grey from the "Filter Data" tab: 
![Grey font](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/145615683-71f7dd88-d255-4299-b744-597234ffd8da.png)

Finally, if we stick to a thin grey font, we could capitalize it all. The idea here is that the size of the font isn't superior to the channel font and that the color doesn't take up attentional resources.
Hi @IanMayo and @ShendMikullovci , I will update when you have a size decision 😄
